# Repository-backed Linux survey

Change `request.txt`, commit and push the session branch, or manually dispatch the workflow on that branch. One Ubuntu runner installs the pinned optional PyNaCl dependency, builds the locked browser client and prepares Chromium, then executes `./test.sh` with the Python and headless-browser encryption tests enabled, then surveys the runner user, a newly created unprivileged user, and root. `runs/linux-permissions.json` contains signal **availability only**, per-signal classifications, selected file modes and whether each user has passwordless sudo, with the run date, kernel and architecture; it contains no identifier values. `runs/latest.log` contains sanitized test output and survey errors. Both are committed directly to the same branch; no artifacts are used. Each new run also saves a run-ID-named copy of its log and survey, allowing results to be compared over time. The result commit does not trigger a second run.

The `ubuntu-latest` runner is one GitHub-hosted virtual machine, not a representative physical Linux desktop or every distribution/sandbox. Runner and isolated-user results may differ because of permissions and group membership. A missing device, unsupported tool, unreadable value or placeholder is reported rather than replaced with an invented ID. Root is tested **only on the disposable runner**; the frontend does not automatically request root.

Only run tests whose stdout/stderr are safe to commit. Never print real identifiers, profiles, credentials, or API keys. Workflow setup failures before the test/survey steps remain in GitHub infrastructure logs and cannot be captured by the repository; a push conflict or disabled write permissions can also prevent saving results. If the branch moves during execution, the job fails instead of overwriting newer work. Actions and `GITHUB_TOKEN` writes must be enabled. The one-runner concurrency setting applies to this workflow, not unrelated workflows. Windows/macOS collectors do not exist yet.

Classifications describe this runner only. `root_only_on_this_runner` means the ordinary process received permission denied and root could read a usable value; it does not imply all Linux systems behave alike. A root-accessible placeholder is classified unavailable. Empty `lsblk` metadata is reported as unavailable/unsupported, not proof that a device is physically absent. The client does not invoke sudo.
